Build the Data MCP and measure the difference

Intermediate 60 minutes Lab 2 of 2
Introduction

In this lab, you'll act as integration engineer for IDEA Brands — building the Data MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that sits between Dana's AI client and Snowflake, then re-running your Lab 1 questions against it.

DK
Dana Kim
RevOps Manager · IDEA Brands

She needs the same five questions answered the same way twice, by a definition somebody signed off on.

The question

What has to sit between the model and the warehouse before you can trust the answer?

You'll learn how to

  • Map three supplied artifacts to the four data design patterns
  • Stand up ideaDataHub reusing only the Snowflake query tool
  • Build three FileStorage-backed skills and attach them as tools
  • Attach ideaDataHub to LibreChat and prove it is the only selected server
  • Re-run the five Lab 1 questions against the completed design and account for the differences

What you'll need

  • Your Lab 1 readings for all five questions — this lab guide already holds them if you are in the same browser you used for Lab 1
  • Your completed Lab 1 handout and your printed Lab 2 handout
  • Your Lab 1 Snowflake Data Explorer MCP server
  • Your assigned pre-provisioned Workato project
  • Access to the event's shared Snowflake connection
  • The supplied design files in FileStorage under DataMCP/ — you'll open them in Phase 1
Phase 1

Read the supplied design

In this phase, you'll map three supplied artifacts to the four data design patterns.

Pattern

Architecture map

The analyst context, the semantic layer, and the verified-query library arrive as one reviewed package. Reading them as configuration — routing rules, stable keys, bounded result contracts — tells you which pattern each one carries, without reading a line of SQL.

1.1

Read what somebody already decided

Lab 1 ended with the model inventing a definition of "needs attention" because nobody had written one down. Somebody has now. Three files carry that work, and none of them require you to read SQL to understand what they are for.

Overview

You end with handout question 1 connecting analyst_context.md, semantic_layer.yaml, and idea_analyst_queries.md to the failures they prevent. Configuration and comments are enough; you do not need to read SQL.

Note

A verified query lets a common question reuse reviewed logic instead of generating SQL again. When none fits, the semantic layer constrains the fallback with approved field meanings, relationships, and filters. Without the first, familiar questions are rebuilt; without the second, unfamiliar questions are guessed from table names.

What to look for
ComponentWhat to inspectPattern it carries
Analyst contextDomain, routing sequence, confidence rules, query rulesSemantic enrichment
Semantic layerSeven course entities, stable keys, Case and Opportunity Contact Role relationshipsRight-sizing
Verified-query libraryNamed business question, definition source, bounded result contract, reviewed SQLPre-aggregation and verification
Detailed steps 6 steps

Reading the design before building it is what keeps the rest of this lab from being copy-typing. Each file removes a decision the raw server left to the model, and the architecture map tells you which evidence to inspect when an answer later takes the exact, adapted, or generated path.

  • In Workato, open FileStorage and open the DataMCP directory from the root.
  • Open analyst_context.md and note the sequence it tells the model to follow when a data question arrives.
  • Open semantic_layer.yaml and note the seven entities, their stable keys, and how a Case relates to an Account.
  • Open idea_analyst_queries.md and note, for one entry, its business question, its definition source, and its result-size bound.
  • Complete handout question 1: for each artifact, name one decision it carries and the Lab 1 failure it addresses.
  • Compare question 1 with a neighbour. If you disagree, one of you has found something in a file the other skimmed.
Verify handout question 1 names one concrete decision and one addressed failure for each supplied file.
Phase 2

Create the MCP server

In this phase, you'll stand up ideaDataHub reusing only the Snowflake query tool.

Pattern

Selective tool reuse

The raw server's whole discovery surface is available to reuse, and you take exactly one tool from it. Everything the model would have used to explore the warehouse is deliberately withheld, and the server instructions supply the sequence it follows instead.

2.1

Create the server and tell it how to behave

The raw server offered the model eight ways to wander the warehouse. This one offers one way to run a query, and a written sequence it has to follow before it gets there.

Overview

You end with an Idea Data Hub folder containing ideaDataHub, one reused execute_query tool, and instructions that name the three retrieval tools you build and attach in Phase 3.

Key insight

Instructions can name tools that do not exist yet

Server instructions are read by the model at connection time, not validated against the tool list. Writing the full sequence now means each skill you attach in Phase 3 slots into a contract that is already in place — and it means a missing tool shows up as a broken sequence rather than a silent gap.

Apply these values
FieldValue
FolderIdea Data Hub, created inside your project
Server typeNew MCP server — start from scratch
SourceProject assets
LocationYour Idea Data Hub folder
Toolsexecute_query from the Snowflake MCP server, and nothing else
Server nameideaDataHub
Server instructionsThe block below, pasted whole
You are a data analyst assistant helping users query and explore data from a Snowflake.

At the start of every session:
1. Call get_analyst_context to load your role and workflow
2. Call get_verified_queries to load pre-validated SQL patterns

For every data question:
3. Understand what the user is asking
4. Check verified queries already loaded from get_verified_queries
   - Exact match → use it (VQR)
   - Close match → adapt it (VQR_ADAPTED)
   - No match → call get_semantic_layer (LLM_GENERATED)
5. Only call get_semantic_layer if no verified query match exists
   Only call get_semantic_layer once per session
6. Call execute_query with the final SQL

IMPORTANT:
- Do not call execute_query first, ever!
- Always use MCP tools only — do not access files directly
- Do not hardcode or assume file names or table names
- Table name is defined in the semantic layer — use it as provided
- Always use ILIKE for text searches
- Always add LIMIT on exploratory queries
- Only query the table defined in the semantic layer
Detailed steps 8 steps

Withholding the discovery tools is the point. If the model can list tables and sample rows, it will, and it will answer from what it found rather than from what was reviewed.

  • In your pre-provisioned project, select Create, then Folder. Name it Idea Data Hub and open it. Everything you build in this lab goes in here.
  • From inside the folder, select Create, then MCP server.
  • Select the New MCP server — Start from scratch to build your own server card.
  • Leave the source on Project assets and confirm Location is your Idea Data Hub folder.
  • Under Add tools from your project, search for execute_query and tick only that tool. Leave every other Snowflake tool unticked.
  • Scroll down and set Server name to ideaDataHub.
  • Paste the instructions block from the config table above into Server instruction. It is a markdown editor, so the numbered lines render as a list — that is expected.
  • Select Start building.
Verify the ideaDataHub overview reads 1 tool, lists execute_query and no other, and that the saved server instructions name get_analyst_context, get_verified_queries, and get_semantic_layer.
Phase 3

Implement the retrieval tools

In this phase, you'll build three FileStorage-backed skills and attach them as tools.

Pattern

FileStorage-backed retrieval

Each retrieval tool is the same three-step recipe: a Start trigger declaring one string response, a FileStorage read, and a Return response step mapping the file contents to it. You build them in the order the model calls them — context, then reviewed queries, then the semantic layer as a fallback — so the build order and the runtime order are the same shape. Building all three is not the same as attaching them, which is why attaching is its own task at the end.

3.1

Give the model its job description

Before the model reads a single table, it needs to know what it is being asked to be: an analyst working a defined domain, with rules about confidence and about what to do when it is unsure. That is what the analyst context carries.

Overview

You end with a running get_analyst_context that returns analyst_context.md as a single string. The template supplies all three steps — a Start trigger declaring one response field, a FileStorage read, and a Return response. All three skills get attached to the server at the end of the phase.

Apply these values
When should this skill run?
Call this at the start of every session.

Returns the analyst role, question workflow, confidence guidance, query rules, required execute_query parameters, and response guidance.

After calling this tool, call get_verified_queries before answering a data question.
FieldValue

File path (Step 2)DataMCP/analyst_context.md

Detailed steps 7 steps

The trigger's response schema is the tool's output contract. If the response field is missing or optional, the Return response step has nothing to map to and the tool returns an empty result the model will happily reason over.

  • In your Idea Data Hub folder, select Create, then Skill. Name it get_analyst_context and select Start building.
  • The skill opens with three steps already in place: a Start trigger, an empty action, and a Return response step. You fill them in; you do not add them.
  • On the Step 1 Start trigger, paste the When should this skill run? text above, keeping its line breaks.
  • Under What information does this skill send back?, select add fields manually. Set Label to context, leave Data type as String, and change Optional from its default of Yes to No. Select Add field.
  • Open Step 2, choose the Workato FileStorage app and the Get file contents action, and set File path to DataMCP/analyst_context.md.
  • Open Step 3 (Return response), select the context field, then select File contents from the Get file contents (Step 2 output) group in the Recipe data panel.
  • Select Save, then Exit, then Start recipe.
Verify the Step 3 mapping chip reads File contents Step 2 — not File name, File path, File size, File creation time, or Last modified time — and that the recipe is running with no failed jobs.
3.2

Give the model the reviewed answers

This is the tool that answers Dana's Monday question the same way twice. The library holds reviewed queries with named business questions and bounded results, so "needs attention" stops being something the model decides in the moment.

Overview

You end with a running get_verified_queries returning idea_analyst_queries.md as one string. Its description carries all four components — when to call it, what it returns, what to check before writing new SQL, and how to label the path it took.

3.3

Give the model the map of the data

The semantic layer is what Lab 1's raw server never had: a statement of which seven entities matter, what their stable keys are, and how a Case connects to an Account. It is the difference between finding a table and knowing it belongs in the answer.

Overview

You end with get_semantic_layer running — the third and last of the three skills. This description is deliberately restrictive — only when no verified query matched, and only once per session — so the model reaches for reviewed logic first. The server still has one tool at the end of this task; attaching all three is Task 3.4.

  • In the same Idea Data Hub folder, select Create, then Skill. Name it get_semantic_layer and select Start building.
  • Paste the When should this skill run? text above into the Step 1 Start trigger, keeping its line breaks.

Verify the Step 3 mapping chip reads File contents Step 2 and the recipe is running, and that the description states both restrictions — only when no verified query matched, and only once per session.
3.4

Hand all three tools to the server

Three skills exist and none of them is on the server yet. This is the step that is easiest to skip and most expensive to skip: a model that cannot see a tool does not report a missing tool, it answers worse.

Overview

You end with ideaDataHub reading 4 tools — execute_query plus the three retrieval skills — with every one of them running. Building a skill and attaching it are two separate acts, and so are attaching it and starting it.

Heads up

A stopped skill attaches without complaint

Each of the last three tasks ended with Start recipe, which is three chances to have missed one. An unstarted skill still attaches to the server and still appears in the tool list — it fails only when the model calls it, and what you see then is LibreChat reporting that the backend tools are not responding. Check all three before you go anywhere near the client.

Phase 4 measures a four-tool server against Lab 1's nine-tool one. If a retrieval tool is missing or stopped, you will still get answers and they will still look plausible — you will be measuring a third design that nobody intended.

  • Return to ideaDataHub and select Add tools.
  • Keep Add from this project, tick all three retrieval skills, and select Add tools.
  • On the server overview, confirm the count now reads 4 tools and that each retrieval tool shows the description you wrote.
  • Confirm all three retrieval skills are running. Any that is not, start it now — an attached tool that is stopped fails at call time, not at attach time.
Verify the ideaDataHub overview reads 4 tools, names execute_query plus all three retrieval skills, shows the description you wrote for each retrieval tool, and that all three retrieval recipes are running.
Phase 4

Connect the enhanced server

In this phase, you'll attach ideaDataHub to LibreChat and prove it is the only selected server.

Pattern

Controlled client attachment

A comparison is only controlled when the client reaches the intended server alone. The capability check and the prompt-bar selector prove the raw Snowflake server cannot participate in the measured runs.

4.1

Put the finished server in front of the client

Four tools sit on the server and none of them have met a model yet. Dana's client is where this either behaves like a data product or repeats Lab 1 with more steps.

Overview

You end with ideaDataHub connected in LibreChat and selected alone, with a capability answer that names the query tool and all three retrieval tools. The prompt-bar selector and that answer together prove the raw Snowflake server did not participate.

Heads up

Prove which server answered

Explain the capabilities of the Idea Data Hub MCP server available in this conversation.

A right answer names the query tool and all three retrieval tools, and is recognisably about your server — reviewed queries, an analyst context, a semantic layer. If it describes a warehouse it can browse, you are still talking to Lab 1's server.

LibreChat will hand you Lab 1's server if you let it. Adding a server adds it to the current selection rather than replacing it, and every fresh conversation opens with the previous selection already applied — so the most likely way to lose this lab is to ask all five questions of the raw Snowflake server again without noticing, get answers that look fine, and compare the baseline against itself. Open the prompt-bar server selector in every fresh conversation and check that Idea Data Hub is the only thing ticked. The capability question is your proof: if the answer does not describe reviewed queries and a semantic layer, fix the selection before you record anything.

Apply these values
FieldValue
Token nameATT<your attendee number>-datahub
LibreChat connection nameIdea Data Hub — <your initials>
TransportStreamable HTTPS
AuthenticationAPI Key, with the credential fields left blank
Detailed steps 7 steps

A fresh conversation is not a formality, and neither is the selector check. Leave both servers selected and the model will mix reviewed retrieval with raw discovery, which is neither design.

  • Open ideaDataHub Settings, then End user access, then Create new token.
  • Name the token ATT<your attendee number>-datahub — your own number, and -datahub to tell it apart from the Lab 1 token you already made. Token names cannot be changed afterwards. Create it, then copy the generated remote MCP URL: it embeds the token, so keep both out of chat messages, handouts, screenshots, and shared notes.
  • In LibreChat, select MCP Settings, then Add MCP, and name the connection Idea Data Hub — <your initials>.
  • Paste the URL and leave Transport on Streamable HTTPS. Set Authentication to API Key and leave the credential fields blank — auto-detect works but is slow enough to cost you measurement time. Select I trust this application, then create the server.
  • In MCP Settings, select Connect for the new server, and select Initialize if LibreChat presents it. Continue once it shows Connected or Active.
  • Open a fresh conversation and open the prompt-bar server selector. The chip will read 2 selected — untick your Lab 1 Snowflake server so only Idea Data Hub remains.
  • Ask the capability question from the Walkthrough above.
Verify the assistant names execute_query, analyst-context retrieval, semantic-layer retrieval, and verified-query retrieval, and that the answer is about your Data Hub rather than about a browsable warehouse. If a tool is missing, return to the server overview and confirm that skill is started and attached.
Phase 5

Re-run and account for the difference

In this phase, you'll re-run the five Lab 1 questions against the completed design and account for the differences.

Pattern

Raw-versus-enhanced comparison

The same five questions, the same wording, fresh conversations, one first answer each. Reliability comes first; completion time, tool calls, and context are supporting evidence. The comparison evaluates the completed design, not any single component's individual contribution.

5.2

Re-run the control

Booked and open pipeline already have narrow meanings, so the raw server may have answered this one well. The enhanced design should not need a dramatic rescue story for a question that was already within reach.

Overview

You end with the Booked & pipeline tab showing Snowflake - Data Explorer beside ideaDataHub, with handout question 3 complete. Treat little or no reliability change as a valid control result, then compare the supporting efficiency readings without inventing a failure.

Detailed steps 3 steps

A comparison where every question improves is one to distrust. This control protects the course claim from becoming "more architecture always makes every answer better."

  • Copy the prompt from Booked & pipeline and send it in a fresh conversation after confirming Idea Data Hub is the only selected server.
  • Record the three enhanced readings in the right-hand column and leave the Lab 1 values unchanged.
  • On handout question 3, record the observed path and source, judge reliability, and state what meaningfully changed — including when the answer did not improve.
Verify Booked & pipeline has separate raw and enhanced readings and handout question 3 treats a defensible no-change result as evidence.

5.5

Put your own question to the new design

The prescribed questions were chosen around known patterns. Your question is the independent row: if it improves, nobody selected it to flatter the design; if it does not, that result matters equally.

Overview

You end with Your question using the wording preserved from Lab 1, new ideaDataHub readings beside the raw ones, and handout question 6 complete. Do not replace the saved wording with a new question here.

Note

Only after the five measured runs

The five measured questions may all resolve as exact reviewed-query matches. That is valid evidence about library coverage, but it does not show what VQR_ADAPTED and LLM_GENERATED mean. After this final measured run, use fresh conversations for two unscored routing probes if you have not observed both paths:

  • Close-match probe: Which customer accounts in manufacturing need attention right now, and why?
  • No-match probe: What is the median age in days of open opportunities, grouped by stage?

Inspect the tool trace and reported sql_generation_type. Record the observed labels on handout question 7 even if they differ from what you expected; do not add the probes as measured runs.

Detailed steps 4 steps

Reusing the wording you authored closes the controlled comparison. Changing it now would measure a new question instead of the new design.

  • Confirm the visible field still contains the question you saved in Lab 1, then copy and send it in a fresh conversation with only Idea Data Hub selected.
  • Record the three enhanced readings in the right-hand column and leave the Lab 1 values unchanged.
  • On handout question 6, record the path and source, judge reliability, and state the meaningful difference from Lab 1.
  • Review handout questions 2 through 6. If you have not observed both an adapted and a generated path, run the two unscored probes from the Aside in fresh conversations and record their labels and trace evidence on question 7.
Verify all five tabs retain read-only raw readings and separate enhanced readings, handout questions 2 through 6 hold the qualitative comparisons, and question 7 records observed or deliberately probed route labels.

Detailed steps 3 steps

The measurement evaluates the completed design as a whole. Claiming that one component produced one effect would overstate what this before-and-after can show, and there is no intermediate condition here to support it.

  • Use handout question 1, your five qualitative comparisons, and the numeric summary below to locate the artifact or observed result behind each pattern.

If you get stuck

  • A retrieval skill returns no content. Confirm the file is in Root directory/DataMCP/, then check the Step 2 path. In Step 3, clear any incorrect chip and select File contents from Step 2 — not file size, creation time, or last-modified time.
  • The assistant does not call get_verified_queries. Check that the tool description names the supported business questions and states when to call it relative to get_analyst_context.
  • The assistant behaves like Lab 1 — browsing tables, inventing definitions. Check the prompt-bar server selector. A fresh conversation keeps the previous selection, so you may be talking to your Lab 1 server. Ask the capability question from Task 4.1 to confirm which one answered.
  • A tool is in the list but never gets called successfully. Confirm that skill's recipe is running. An attached skill that is stopped fails at call time, and LibreChat reports it as the backend tools not responding.
  • The answer does not match what you expected. Record whether the assistant adapted a reviewed query rather than using it as-is, and confirm you are on the pinned event snapshot.
  • A LibreChat measurement is not visible. Leave that figure unavailable rather than estimating it. Workato job history may explain the run, but it does not replace the field with an estimate.

Reflect

Now that you have both designs measured against the same five questions, consider what you would have to defend if this went to Dana's team on Monday.

  • Your enhanced answer used a reviewed query. Who reviewed it, how would you know if it went stale, and what happens the first time the business changes the definition?
  • The three retrieval tools are read-only and return whole files. What breaks first as the query library grows to two hundred entries?
  • get_semantic_layer is described as a last resort. What would you expect to see in the trace if the model started reaching for it on every question, and what would that tell you?
  • One question probably improved less than the others. Was that the question, the library, or the measurement — and what evidence separates those three?

Wrap-up

Dana asks the same question on Monday and gets the same answer she got last Monday, from a definition somebody signed off on, with a trace that says which query produced it.

Patterns to carry forward:

  • Subtract tools deliberately. One query tool plus a written sequence beats a full discovery surface, because the model answers from what is reviewed rather than from what it found.
  • The response schema is the output contract. A missing or optional response field produces a tool that succeeds and returns nothing, and the model will reason over the nothing.
  • Descriptions route as well as document. Naming when not to call a tool is how you keep a fallback path from becoming the default one.
  • Provenance labels make reliability checkable. VQR, VQR_ADAPTED, and LLM_GENERATED are the difference between an answer you trust and an answer you like.

Going further — extend the query library

This extension is optional and carries no required objective. Take it only if you can read and adapt a supplied SQL query, work with a CTE, and reason through an undeclared two-hop join. Work only in your own project — the supplied library file is shared, so you will extend what your tool returns rather than editing the file itself.

  1. Ask: Which attention-candidate accounts have open deals without an Executive Sponsor?
  2. Use the supplied definition — an open Opportunity has confirmed sponsorship only when SALESFORCE_OPPORTUNITYCONTACTROLE holds an Executive Sponsor role for that Opportunity ID.
  3. Find the closest supplied query in the library.
  4. Adapt it along the OPPORTUNITYCONTACTROLE → OPPORTUNITY → ACCOUNT path without changing the attention threshold.
  5. Check that it groups by stable IDs, preserves exclusions, and stays inside the result-size guard.
  6. Test it before you commit to it. You have no Snowflake console, but you do have a query tool — in a fresh conversation, ask your Data Hub to run the SQL exactly as you wrote it and tell you what came back. Read-only work only: this is the event's shared warehouse.
  7. Add it to what the tool returns, not to the file. Open get_verified_queries and go to the Return response step. Keep the File contents datapill where it is, and type your new entry after it — the field takes literal text alongside a datapill, so the tool now returns the supplied library plus your addition, with no write access needed anywhere. Match the format of the entries already in the file, or the model will not read yours as a library entry.
  8. Save, Exit, and Start recipe again. Nothing you changed reaches the server until you do.
  9. Re-run the question in a fresh conversation and record the result alongside your other readings. Check the trace: if the model reports a reviewed-query path rather than generating SQL from the semantic layer, your entry is being read as part of the library.

Step 7 is the idea worth keeping. A retrieval tool's output is something you compose, not only something you fetch — which means you can extend a reviewed library you have no permission to edit, and it means you own the contract your tool returns.
